   256	let align_normalized query target =
   257	  let rec align offset target =
   258	    match Util.Smith_waterman.align Util.Smith_waterman.code query target with
   259	    | None -> None
   260	    | Some aligned ->
   261	        let start, end_ =
   262	          Util.Text.safe_range target ~start:aligned.target.start
   263	            ~end_:aligned.target.end_
   264	        in
   265	        if start = aligned.target.start && end_ = aligned.target.end_ then
   266	          Some
   267	            {
   268	              aligned with
   269	              target = { start = offset + start; end_ = offset + end_ };
   270	            }
   271	        else if start >= end_ then None
   272	        else align (offset + start) (String.sub target start (end_ - start))
   273	  in
   274	  align 0 target

   276	let align_candidate ~query ~normalized_query (meta : T.doc_meta) contents hits

   278	  let mode_offset = most_common_offset hits in
   279	  let selected =
   280	    List.filter
   281	      (fun hit ->
   282	        abs (hit.query_start - hit.doc_start - mode_offset)
   283	        <= match_offset_tolerance)
   284	      hits
   285	  in
   286	  let start, end_ =
   287	    List.fold_left
   288	      (fun (start, end_) hit ->
   289	        (min start hit.doc_start, max end_ hit.doc_end))
   290	      (String.length contents, 0)
   291	      selected
   292	  in
   293	                                                                           
   294	                                                                          
   295	                                                                            
   296	  let start = min start (max 0 (-mode_offset)) in
   297	  let end_ =
   298	    max end_
   299	      (min (String.length contents) (String.length query - mode_offset))
   300	  in
   301	  let window =
   302	    {
   303	      T.start = max 0 (start - shingle_length);
   304	      end_ = min (String.length contents) (end_ + shingle_length);
   305	    }
   306	  in
   307	  let start, end_ =
   308	    Util.Text.safe_range contents ~start:window.start ~end_:window.end_
   309	  in
   310	  let window = { T.start; end_ } in
   311	                                                                          
   312	                                                                                
   313	  let maximum_window =
   314	    String.length query + (2 * match_offset_tolerance) + (2 * shingle_length)
   315	  in
   316	  if window.end_ - window.start > maximum_window then None

   485	  let query_shingles, minimum_hits, rejected, candidates =

   493	        ~doc_revision_attempt:doc_revision;
   494	      None
   495	  | candidate :: _ ->
   496	      let range = candidate.range in
   497	      let raw_contents =
   498	        String.sub candidate.contents range.start (range.end_ - range.start)
   499	      in
   500	      let changed =
   501	        candidate.doc_id <> a.doc_id
   502	        || range <> a.range
   503	        || raw_contents <> a.raw_contents
   504	      in

   510	          doc_revision_attempt = candidate.revision;

I found three potential issues:

- **P0 — An unchanged anchor can move to an unrelated copy.** Relocation ranks candidates by shingle coverage, then hit count, then document ID, with no preference for the anchor’s current document ([Anchor.ml](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-stripped-comments-markdown/base-libs/text/Anchor.ml:348)). If an earlier-indexed file contains the same passage, updating the original file can silently move its anchor to that copy even when the passage remains intact in the original. That changes what document the anchor cites.

- **P1 — A failed relocation is not retried when the destination arrives later.** Failed attempts record the current revision ([Anchor.ml](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-stripped-comments-markdown/base-libs/text/Anchor.ml:490)), while updates only retry anchors belonging to the document being updated ([DB.ml](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-stripped-comments-markdown/base-libs/text/DB.ml:852)). If the old file is removed before its replacement is indexed, adding the replacement leaves the anchor outdated until the old document changes again.

- **P1 — A one-byte insertion can orphan a minimum-length anchor.** Document shingles are indexed only at eight-byte intervals ([Anchor.ml](/workspace/kb-research/samples/skeletor/skeletor-stripped-comments-markdown/base-libs/text/Anchor.ml:167)). A 16-byte anchor has only one possible shingle; inserting one byte before it shifts that shingle off the indexed positions, so relocation finds no candidate despite an exact match.
